case.case_title: Lalith Deshapriya v Captain Weerakoon and Others
case.court_name: Court of Appeal of Sri Lanka

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was detained without being brought before a judge or without a legal order, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that he was detained unlawfully without being produced before a judicial authority or having a legal order authorizing his detention.
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents did not provide evidence that the petitioner was brought before a judge or that his detention was authorized by a legal order.
key_facts: Petitioner was detained from 4th September 2001 to 8th January 2002 under close arrest.
No evidence was presented that petitioner was brought before a judge during detention.
Petitioner was subjected to torture and coercion during detention.
Summary trial was conducted by the commanding officer without proper legal safeguards.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) mandates that any detained person must be brought before a judge and cannot be held without a legal order. The court found that the petitioner was detained for an extended period without judicial oversight or legal authorization.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner’s prolonged detention without being produced before a judge or having a legal order violated Article 13(2), undermining the legality of the detention and subsequent trial.
principles_established: Detention without judicial oversight or legal order is unlawful under Article 13(2).
Prolonged detention without judicial review violates fundamental rights.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s detention violated Article 13(2) and contributed to the nullity of the summary trial and conviction.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The conviction and dismissal were quashed and the petitioner was ordered to be re-enlisted.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) is central because it protects detainees from unlawful detention without judicial oversight, which was a key factor in the court’s decision to quash the proceedings.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was kept under close arrest for months without being brought before a judge or having a legal order authorizing detention, violating Article 13(2).
